# Bhaddekaratta Sutta (MN 131 (PTS MN iii 187))

**ID:** MN 131 (PTS MN iii 187)  
**Section:** Majjhimanikāya (mn)  
**Collection:** Sutta  
**Title (Pali):** Bhaddekaratta Sutta  
**Title (English, from literature):** One Fine Night  
**PTS:** MN iii 187  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0203m.mul3.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0203m.mul3.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Bhaddekaratta Sutta* (MN 131) is the opening discourse of a group of four consecutive *Bhaddekaratta* suttas located in the *Vibhaṅgavagga* of the *Uparipaṇṇāsa* in the *Majjhimanikāya* [Holz 2009; Skilling 2001]. The sutta begins with a summary (*uddesa*) consisting of a concise set of verses urging the practitioner not to revive the past, build hopes on the future, or become embroiled in the present, but rather to see things as they are and cultivate insight with present effort [Rogell 2003]. The Buddha then provides a detailed exposition (*vibhaṅga*) explaining these verses through the framework of the five aggregates (*khandha*), demonstrating that reviving the past or yearning for the future consists in finding delight in one's aggregates, whereas one avoids being bound up in the present by not identifying the five aggregates as self [Rogell 2003; Buswell & Lopez 2014]. Traditional commentary interprets the enigmatic title term *bhaddekaratta* as "one who is happy [auspicious] for one single night" (*bhaddakassa ekarattassa*) owing to insight, reflected also in Chinese renderings meaning "a good night" (*shanye*), while modern translators have rendered it as "An Exposition of the Bhaddekaratta Sutta / Ideal Solitude" and "Knowing the Better Way to Live Alone" [Buswell & Lopez 2014; Ñāṇananda 1973; Thich Nhat Hanh 1998].

**Parallels and text reuse**

- Full parallels: SHT Sutta 21
- Passage-level parallels: Sag Śarīrārthagāthā; MN 132 (PTS MN iii 189) Ānandabhaddekaratta Sutta; MN 133 (PTS MN iii 192) Mahākaccānabhaddekaratta Sutta; MN 134 (PTS MN iii 199) Lomasakaṅgiyabhaddekaratta Sutta
- Resembling parallels: Ja 538 Mūgapakkhajātaka
- Mentioned in: Ne 37 Sāsanapaṭṭhāna; Tha-Ap 550 Lomasakaṅgiyattheraapadāna; Mnd 10 Purābhedasuttaniddesa; Mnd 9 Māgaṇḍiyasuttaniddesa

**Sources**

- [Holz 2009] Holz, The Bhadrakarātrī-sūtra: Apotropaic Scriptures in Early Indian Buddhism — Discussion of textual transmission, Sanskrit fragments with dhāraṇīs, the Vibhaṅgavagga's composition, and Madhyama-āgama parallels.
- [Skilling 2001] Skilling, 'Dharma, Dhāraṇī, Abhidharma, Avadāna: What was taught in Trayastriṃśa' (2001) — Contextualization of the four Bhaddekaratta discourses in the Uparipaṇṇāsa and note of the title verses.
- [Rogell 2003] Rogell, Pressing Out Pure Honey: A Practitioner's Study Guide (Majjhima Nikāya) (2003) — Summary of MN 131's verses, thematic core, and exposition via the five aggregates.
- [Buswell & Lopez 2014] Buswell & Lopez, The Princeton Dictionary of Buddhism (2014) — Commentarial gloss on bhaddekaratta/bhaddakassa ekarattassa, Chinese rendering shanye, and skandha analysis.
- [Ñāṇananda 1973] Bhikkhu Ñāṇananda, Ideal Solitude: An Exposition of the Bhaddekaratta Sutta (1973), cited in Ñāṇamoli & Bodhi (1995) — Translation title and dedicated study of MN 131.
- [Thich Nhat Hanh 1998] Thich Nhat Hanh, The Heart of the Buddha's Teaching (1998) — Alternative English title for MN 131.
- [Hazra 1994] Hazra, Pāli Language and Literature (1994) — Brief summary of the sutta's emphasis on the present rather than the past or future.
- [Lee 2017] Lee, A Study of the Śarīrārthagāthā in the Yogācārabhūmi (2017) — Comparison of the verses in MN 131–134 with verse sets in the Yogācārabhūmi.
